decision.body: Rows show mobility; columns show the decision layer. Bubble area follows mentions coded to each finding.
decision.matrixLabel: Three by four semantic matrix of findings by mobility and layer

decision.tooltipFrequencyShort: {frequency, plural, one {# mention supports this finding} other {# mentions support this finding}}

brief.title: What the brand can decide
brief.moreActions: {count, plural, one {# additional linked action} other {# additional linked actions}}
brief.noActionTitle: No linked action in this release
brief.noActionBody: The finding remains valid, but the governed analysis did not attach an execution card. No recommendation is inferred in the interface.

empty.title: No active findings in this period
empty.body: The published study is available, but no finding has coded presence inside the selected dates. Try a broader period.

balance.title: Period mix by decision layer
balance.body: Counts of all {count, number} active findings in {period}. The selected finding only highlights its layer.
balance.chartLabel: Diverging trigger and barrier finding counts by layer
balance.denominator: Denominator: {count, number} findings. Mixed findings are listed in the table.

presence.title: Coded mentions by month
presence.tooltipCount: {count, plural, one {# coded mention} other {# coded mentions}}
presence.denominator: Distinct snapshot mentions coded to this finding in the month.

evidenceChain.label: Relationship between mentions and evidence
evidenceChain.explanation: A coded mention contributes to finding frequency. Only reviewed citations become evidence links; each link opens one source publication in Mentions.

index.title: Choose a finding to read
index.body: The {count, number} findings and their evidence remain bound to the same published cut.
index.meta: {evidence, plural, one {# evidence link} other {# evidence links}} · {frequency, number} coded mentions

drawer.label: Evidence for {finding}
drawer.body: These are the {count, plural, one {# reviewed mention supporting} other {# reviewed mentions supporting}} this finding. Open the enriched record to review its full context.
drawer.empty: No evidence mentions are available for this finding.

errors.finding: The selected finding could not be loaded.
errors.evidence: The evidence could not be loaded.
errors.period: The selected period could not be loaded.

activeFindings.title: Active findings
activeFindings.body: Ideas from the study that appear at least once in the period's conversations.
activeFindings.reading: This counts findings, not mentions. One finding may be supported by many conversations.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.body: Findings that help a person move toward a decision or action.
triggers.reading: Use them to see what the brand should make easier, reinforce, or make more visible.

barriers.title: Barriers
barriers.body: Findings that slow down, complicate, or create doubt during a decision.
barriers.reading: Use them to spot friction the brand can remove or reduce.

directAction.title: Direct action
directAction.body: Findings the brand has enough control over to address now.
directAction.reading: This does not make them the automatic priority; it identifies where an immediate response is possible.

codedCoverage.title: Coded coverage
codedCoverage.body: Share of distinct source mentions in the selected period that were assigned to at least one governed finding.
codedCoverage.reading: Calculation: coded mentions ÷ published mentions × 100. Use it to judge how much of the period can support the decision field.

evidenceCoverage.title: Evidence coverage
evidenceCoverage.body: Share of active findings with at least one reviewed citation in the selected period.
evidenceCoverage.reading: Calculation: active findings with evidence ÷ all active findings × 100. It measures support across findings, not the number of citations.

evidenceLinks.title: Evidence links
evidenceLinks.body: Reviewed finding-to-mention citation links attached to active findings and dated inside the selected window.
evidenceLinks.reading: Calculation: sum of their curated links. It changes with dates; open Evidence to read the linked source records.

movability.title: Movable findings
movability.body: Share of findings present in the selected period that are classified as directly movable by the brand.
movability.reading: Calculation: movable active findings ÷ all active findings × 100. It changes when the active set changes; use it to size immediate action.

population.title: Published mentions
population.body: Distinct source publications in the frozen release snapshot whose publication date falls inside the selected window.
population.reading: It changes with dates and provides the period population. Not every published mention is coded to a finding or promoted as evidence.

decisionField.title: How to read the Decision field
decisionField.body: Each bubble is a finding. Columns show which part of the decision it affects; rows show how much control the brand has. Green moves people forward and red holds them back.
decisionField.reading: Area is proportional to coded mentions and bubbles are ordered from highest to lowest volume within each quadrant. Governed priority is shown separately.

denominator.title: What frequency means
denominator.body: The period contains {count, number} mentions classified for this study. Each bubble uses only the mentions that support that finding.
denominator.reading: One conversation may support more than one finding, so do not add bubbles as if they represented different people.

movible_por_marca.title: Act on it
movible_por_marca.body: The brand can change this condition directly, for example through price, service, communication, or process.
movible_por_marca.reading: Look here for decisions that can become a concrete short-term intervention.

parcialmente_movible.title: Shape it
parcialmente_movible.body: The brand can influence this condition, but moving it requires consistency and time.
parcialmente_movible.reading: Look here for expectations, perceptions, or habits that will not change through one action.

estructural.title: Respect it
estructural.body: The condition comes from the category, context, or culture and is not under the brand's direct control.
estructural.reading: Use it as a constraint or context for adapting strategy, not as a promise of immediate change.

ranking.title: Priority findings
ranking.body: Active findings ordered by the governed composite priority score, with coded mentions used only as a tie-breaker.
ranking.reading: The score combines the study's reviewed decision dimensions. Selecting a row updates the same brief, reading, and evidence.

layerMix.title: Period mix by decision layer
layerMix.body: Counts active findings—not mentions—by trigger, barrier, or mixed polarity in every matrix column.
layerMix.reading: It changes with the date-filtered active set. Selecting a finding highlights its layer but does not filter the other layer totals.

findingIndex.title: Finding index
findingIndex.body: The release finding list, restricted to findings with observed presence in the selected period.
findingIndex.reading: Choose one finding to keep its reading and governed evidence synchronized.

frequency.title: Coded mentions
frequency.body: Distinct snapshot mentions assigned to this finding inside the selected period.
frequency.reading: One mention may support more than one finding, so finding totals are not additive.

priority.title: Priority
priority.body: Governed composite score combining decision relevance, ability to act, and support for the finding.
priority.reading: It orders the findings list. Mention volume is shown separately and only breaks ties between equal scores.

findingEvidence.title: Evidence links
findingEvidence.body: Reviewed citations connected to this finding and present in the selected period.
findingEvidence.reading: Open Evidence to inspect each cited mention once.

intensity.title: Intensity
intensity.body: Average intensity of mention-level codings for this finding in the selected period.
intensity.reading: Higher values indicate stronger expression, not necessarily more mentions.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.body: Governed confidence assigned to the published finding during review.
confidence.reading: Confidence qualifies the interpretation; it is not recalculated by the date filter.

presence.title: Coded mentions by month
presence.body: Distinct relational mention codings for the selected finding, grouped by publication month inside the selected period.
presence.reading: The monthly points sum to the finding's coded-mention count for the window; evidence links are a reviewed subset and can be fewer.

evidencePreview.title: Governed evidence preview
evidencePreview.body: The first five stable citations for the selected finding and period.
evidencePreview.reading: Open the drawer for cursor-paginated evidence or open a mention for its enriched record.

personal.title: Personal
personal.body: What a person experiences practically while deciding: price, access, service, time, or convenience.
personal.reading: Example: an offer fits their budget, or a delivery takes too long.

psicologico.title: Psychological
psicologico.body: What the person believes or feels: trust, risk, perceived value, safety, or expectation.
psicologico.reading: Example: they fear an offer is misleading, or feel that the brand understands them.

social.title: Social
social.body: How other people shape the decision through recommendations, reviews, communities, or group norms.
social.reading: Example: a recommendation from other pet owners reduces doubt.

cultural.title: Cultural
cultural.body: Shared habits and meanings that reach beyond one person or purchase.
cultural.reading: Example: established expectations about how a pet should be cared for.

filters.equalWindow: The comparison automatically uses the preceding window with the same number of days.

comparison.label: Compare with
comparison.noOverlap: The comparison cannot overlap the primary period.
comparison.equalDays: Select exactly {count} days to keep the comparison equivalent.

dataScope.body: Brand Monitoring reads this workspace's approved primary-brand mentions. Studies do not change the population visible to the client.

topicsNarratives.title: Topics and narratives
topicsNarratives.subtitle: See what people discuss, which narratives gain ground, and open the evidence to decide where to investigate or act.

partial.title: This view is still useful, with declared partial coverage
partial.body: {classified, number} of {included, number} mentions are classified. {pending, number} still need processing or review and are excluded from client-safe metrics.

insights.budgetHelp: Reads up to {limit, number} governed mentions and approved context. Maximum budget: {budget}.
insights.error: Could not complete the Topics & Narratives investigation.
insights.emptyBody: Run a governed investigation of up to {limit, number} mentions from the latest thirty days, capped at {budget}. Every analyzed mention remains enriched in Data OS.
insights.pendingBody: Claude is reading {analyzed, number} of {population, number} eligible mentions, approved internal context and bounded external sources.
insights.noFindings: The investigation read {analyzed, number} mentions but found no non-obvious pattern with enough evidence to publish.

ranking.mapReading: Each bubble is a term. Horizontal position shows supporting mentions, vertical position shows observed interactions on a logarithmic scale, and size shows share of the period.
ranking.mapReadingNoComparison: Each bubble is a term. Horizontal position shows supporting mentions, vertical position shows observed interactions on a logarithmic scale, and size shows share of the period.

detail.title: Select a term
detail.notAvailable: We could not load this term's detail. The ranking remains available and you can try another period.
detail.sentimentMix: {positive, number} positive · {neutral, number} neutral · {negative, number} negative
detail.sentimentCaveat: The term is not inherently positive or negative. This balance describes the tone of its supporting evidence.
detail.compositionBody: Approved evidence excerpts; open the detail to review every mention.
detail.additionalEvidence: {count, plural, one {# more mention} other {# more mentions}}
detail.sourceSummary: {mentions, number} source mentions across {batches, number} import batches

charts.otherNarratives: Narratives present in the selected period
charts.otherTopics: Topics present in the selected period

cooccurrence.title: Terms that appear together
cooccurrence.empty: There is not enough evidence to show associations above the expected base rate in this period.
cooccurrence.navigationHint: Drag to move · scroll to zoom
cooccurrence.listBody: Pairs shown share at least two mentions and occur at least 1.1× as often as expected from each term's base rate. This is association, not causality.
cooccurrence.selectedEmpty: This term has no association above the minimum evidence and base-rate threshold.
cooccurrence.sharedMentions: {count, plural, one {# shared mention} other {# shared mentions}}
cooccurrence.termMentions: {count, plural, one {# supporting mention} other {# supporting mentions}}

evidence.title: Source evidence
evidence.body: These are the mentions behind this term. Open any original to review its full context.
evidence.empty: No evidence mentions are available for this term.

empty.title: No approved terms in this view
empty.body: Change the period or filters. Pending and rejected classifications remain excluded from client-safe results.

errors.detail: Could not load the selected term.

coverage.title: Classified coverage
coverage.body: The share of included mentions that currently have at least one approved term in this lens.
coverage.reading: Higher coverage means the map represents more of the selected conversation. Partial coverage is disclosed rather than filled with assumptions.

terms.title: Active terms
terms.body: The approved terms from the active governed profile that appear at least once in the selected view.
terms.reading: A larger count means more variety, not necessarily a better or worse result.

assertions.title: Tag assertions
assertions.body: Approved links between source mentions and topic or narrative terms. One mention can support more than one term.
assertions.reading: This is why assertions can be higher than classified mentions; it is not a count of unique people or posts.

pending.title: Pending mentions
pending.body: Included mentions whose classification is still processing or waiting for governed review.
pending.reading: They are not silently treated as unclassified and do not enter client-safe term counts until approved.

topic.title: Topics
topic.body: Topics answer what people are discussing: a product, service, need, event, problem or subject found in the source conversation.
topic.reading: Use volume and share to see prominence. A topic can rise without implying positive or negative meaning.

narrative.title: Narratives
narrative.body: Narratives answer what story, belief or interpretive frame people are building around the subjects they discuss.
narrative.reading: Unlike a topic, a narrative is a claim or frame. Read it with its evidence before treating it as a strategic conclusion.

trend.title: Term movement
trend.body: Shows how many approved source mentions supported the selected term in each interval of the chosen period.
trend.reading: Use the shape to distinguish a sustained pattern from a one-day spike, then open evidence to understand why it moved.

interpretation.title: How to read the term
interpretation.body: Combines its governed definition, period relevance, sentiment mix, evolution and source evidence.
interpretation.reading: It does not automatically assign an owner or turn the term into a risk. Use tone and evidence to decide whether brand, product, experience or service should act.

supportingMentions.title: Supporting mentions
supportingMentions.body: Unique source mentions linked to this term in the selected period.
supportingMentions.reading: Open the evidence to see exactly which conversations are counted.

periodShare.title: Share of the period
periodShare.body: The percentage of included, classified mentions in this lens that support the selected term.
periodShare.reading: Use it to judge prominence within this view; it is not market share.

sentimentEvidence.title: Evidence sentiment
sentimentEvidence.body: The positive, neutral and negative tone of the source mentions supporting this term.
sentimentEvidence.reading: The term itself is not inherently positive or negative. Read this mix with the evidence to decide whether it represents momentum, friction or a mixed signal.

cooccurrence.title: Association network
cooccurrence.body: Compares observed co-occurrence with the amount expected from each term's base rate, using only approved source mentions.
cooccurrence.reading: Line width shows shared mentions; the side list shows pairs with at least two shared mentions that occur at least 1.1× more often than expected. This is exploratory association, not causality or proof of correlation.

mentions.title: Mentions
mentions.subtitle: Explore the approved conversation behind {brand}, with its governed context attached.

search.label: Search mentions
search.placeholder: Search words or an exact phrase

columns.title: Columns
columns.required: Mention is required and cannot be hidden.

mentions.selection: {count, plural, one {# mention selected} other {# mentions selected}}
mentions.selectionAll: Select all mentions on this page
mentions.selectionClearAll: Clear all mentions on this page

scope.help: Shows which listening scope found the mention: brand, competitor or category. It does not mean the post was authored by an official brand account.

tb.title: Triggers & Barriers classification
tb.reviewNote: The role and decision layer are structured T&B classifications. Observed signals are short evidence phrases found in the mention; they are not a separate taxonomy.

empty.title: No mentions match this view
empty.body: Change the period, search or filters to widen the conversation.

detail.title: Mention detail
detail.noText: This record has no client-visible text.
detail.noEnrichment: No approved topic or narrative is attached to this mention yet.

scope.title: What source scope means
scope.body: The listening scope that captured this mention: brand, competitor or category. It describes why the record entered the data, not who authored it.
scope.process: Assigned during ingestion from the approved source and query catalog. A mention can match more than one scope.

tb.title: Where T&B comes from
tb.body: A structured decision classification from the most recent Triggers & Barriers analysis approved by a Noisia analyst.
tb.process: New mentions remain without this label until they are included in a new T&B coding run and that analysis is approved.

enrichment.title: What enriched context is
enrichment.body: Approved topics, narratives, entities and other governed tags attached to the mention so it can be grouped and traced beyond keyword matching.
enrichment.process: Populated by Data OS enrichment and human review. It can update independently from the T&B analysis.

attributes.title: What analyzed attributes are
attributes.body: Typed features detected or calculated for this record by an approved analysis or ETL step.
attributes.process: Detected means the boolean feature exists for this mention. It is not a quality score or an approval by itself.

observedSignals.title: What an observed signal is
observedSignals.body: A short evidence phrase that summarizes what is happening in this exact mention, such as a misleading promotion or a registration problem.
observedSignals.process: It is produced during open T&B coding and remains linked to the approved analysis and original mention.

filterControls.title: Controls
filterControls.searchHelp: Searches the included mention text and recalculates every metric in this view.
filterControls.summary: {count, plural, =0 {No active filters} one {# active filter} other {# active filters}}
filterControls.facetsError: Available filters could not be loaded.
filterControls.noFacets: There are no governed dimensions available for this period.

insight.label: Useful information
insight.pending: Period volume is still being materialized
insight.volume: {count} mentions in the period ({delta} vs. previous)
insight.context: Compared with {previous}; open the evidence to understand the movement.
insight.noComparison: Showing the selected period without a comparison.

monthlyInsights.fixedWindow: Fixed window; report filters do not change it

refresh.error: We could not update the monthly insights.
refresh.help: Analyzes the last 30 days with the study's approved context. Live charts remain available while it runs.

up.headline: Conversation grew {delta} to {count} mentions
up.explanation: The period closed with {current} mentions versus {previous} in the prior 30 days ({delta}).

down.headline: Conversation fell {delta} to {count} mentions
down.explanation: The period closed with {current} mentions versus {previous} in the prior 30 days ({delta}).

steady.headline: Conversation held near {count} mentions
steady.explanation: Volume was {current} mentions versus {previous} in the previous window ({delta}).

volume.noComparison: {count} mentions are available; there is not yet a complete previous window to compare.
volume.chartAria: Daily conversation volume in the last 30 days

concentration.headline: Three conversations explain {share} of monthly volume
concentration.explanation: These conversations contain {count} mentions. A high share means the movement depends on a few threads and should be checked in the evidence.
concentration.chartAria: Conversations with the largest number of mentions

up.headline: {share} of mentions are comments
up.explanation: The comment share increased: more activity is happening inside existing threads than in posts starting new conversations.

down.headline: {share} of mentions are comments
down.explanation: The comment share fell: the period depends relatively more on new posts than replies inside the same thread.

steady.headline: {share} of mentions are comments
steady.explanation: The mix of posts starting conversations and comments stayed without a meaningful change.

depth.chartAria: Comparison of original posts and comments

positive.headline: Net sentiment balance is {balance} points
positive.explanation: The calculation uses {count} classified mentions. A positive value means positive mentions outweigh negative ones.

negative.headline: Net sentiment balance is {balance} points
negative.explanation: The calculation uses {count} classified mentions. A negative value means negative mentions outweigh positive ones.

balanced.headline: Net sentiment balance is {balance} points
balanced.explanation: The calculation uses {count} classified mentions. A value near zero means a similar mix of positive and negative conversation.

sentiment.chartAria: Sentiment distribution in the last 30 days

platform.headline: {platform} concentrates {share} of monthly mentions
platform.explanation: Origin is calculated over {count} observed mentions. High concentration means the result depends especially on that channel.
platform.chartAria: Platforms with the most mentions in the last 30 days

up.headline: Posts generated {count} interactions, up {delta}
up.explanation: {current} interactions were observed versus {previous} in the previous window ({delta}).

down.headline: Posts generated {count} interactions, down {delta}
down.explanation: {current} interactions were observed versus {previous} in the previous window ({delta}).

steady.explanation: {current} interactions were observed versus {previous} in the previous window ({delta}).

mentions.title: Mentions
mentions.body: Every public item captured in the selected period that matches the monitored brand or topic. A mention may be an original publication or a comment.
mentions.reading: Mentions measure how much content exists. They do not equal unique people: one person can create several mentions.

conversations.title: Conversations
conversations.body: Distinct discussions. One conversation groups the publication that started it and every comment linked to that publication.
conversations.reading: More conversations means more independent discussions. Many mentions inside few conversations means the volume is concentrated.

root_posts.title: Root posts
root_posts.body: Original publications that start a conversation. Replies and comments are not counted here.
root_posts.reading: They show how many independent starting points generated discussion, not how many responses each one received.

comments.title: Comments
comments.body: Responses attached to an original publication. Every comment is also a mention, but it does not start a new conversation.
comments.reading: Many comments signal a deep or contested discussion. They do not necessarily mean that many independent conversations exist.

volume.title: Volume over time
volume.aria: Conversation volume for the current period compared with the previous period
volume.ariaNoComparison: Conversation volume for the selected period

help.title: Volume over time
help.body: Shows how many mentions, conversations, original publications or comments appeared in each interval of the selected period.
help.reading: Use the previous-period line as a baseline. Change units to tell broad growth across many discussions from a spike caused by one heavily commented publication.

sentiment.title: Sentiment distribution
sentiment.coverage: {classified} of {total} mentions have a classifiable sentiment.

help.title: Sentiment distribution
help.body: Groups the mentions whose tone can be identified as positive, neutral or negative. Mentions without a reliable tone stay outside the donut.
help.reading: Check the classified count below the chart before drawing conclusions. A negative share is more important when it represents many mentions, not only a large percentage of a small base.

composition.title: How the conversation is composed
composition.aria: Composition of root posts and comments over time

help.title: How the conversation is composed
help.body: Separates original publications, which start a conversation, from comments, which continue an existing conversation.
help.reading: More original publications usually means broader spread. More comments means deeper discussion or concentration around fewer starting points. Use sentiment to know whether that depth helps or hurts the brand.

help.title: Sentiment balance over time
help.body: Condenses the difference between positive and negative conversation into one value from −100 to +100. Neutral mentions count in the base but do not push the value up or down.
help.formula: Sentiment balance = (positive mentions − negative mentions) ÷ classified mentions × 100
help.reading: Above zero means positive mentions outweigh negative ones; below zero means the opposite. A rising balance is favorable only when enough mentions were classified, so always check volume and coverage.

help.title: Where the conversation comes from
help.body: Shows how many captured mentions came from each channel during the selected period.
help.reading: Use it to see whether a movement is broad or driven by one channel. A large bar means more observed conversation there, not automatically better brand performance.

engagement.title: Observed engagement
engagement.note: Only observed components are summed; missing fields are not estimated.

attention.title: Root post performance
attention.note: Calculated only across {count} root posts; comments do not inflate engagement or views.

help.title: Root post performance
help.body: Measures attention received by original publications only. Comments are excluded so a long discussion does not make the starting publication look stronger than it was.
help.reading: Median is the typical post: half received less and half received more. The 90th percentile is not a score; it is the level reached by only the top 10% of posts. If it rises while the median stays flat, a few posts are concentrating attention. “Posts with interaction” is the share with at least one reaction. View coverage shows how many posts supplied that data. Green or red means the metric rose or fell versus the previous period—not that the conversation was positive or negative.

help.title: Detected emotions
help.body: Groups mentions by the emotion expressed in their text, such as joy, anger or concern.
help.reading: This describes the language in the conversation, not the identity or personality of the people posting. Open the evidence to verify the context.

topics.title: Active topics and narratives
topics.empty: No governed topics are available for this period yet.

help.title: Active topics and narratives
help.body: Topics are the subjects being discussed. Narratives are recurring ways people explain or frame those subjects.
help.reading: A larger share means the topic or narrative occupies more of the selected conversation. Growth shows attention, not whether it benefits the brand; combine it with sentiment and evidence.

drivers.title: Conversations that explain volume
drivers.subtitle: Each bar groups one original publication and every comment attached to it.
drivers.aria: Conversation ranking by number of mentions in each discussion

help.title: Conversations that explain volume
help.body: Ranks complete conversations by adding the original publication and every comment attached to it.
help.reading: A large bar means one discussion explains a meaningful part of the period’s volume. This is concentration, not reach. Open it to see whether it is an opportunity, an issue or irrelevant noise.

help.title: Highlighted conversations

help.reading: These examples explain the aggregate but do not represent every mention. Open the original item before using it in a decision or report.
